newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-POLICE CHIEF DENIES CLAIM OF EXCESSIVE FORCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-POLICE CHIEF DENIES CLAIM OF EXCESSIVE FORCE.

text.p: Oporto police chief Delfim Passos has denied claims that his men used excessive force after eight Manchester United fans were injured by anti-riot pellets following Wednesday's European Cup quarter-final against Porto.
The injured, including one fan with head wounds, were taken to hospital but all were discharged in the early hours of Thursday, British consular officials said.
Angry United fans returning to Britain accused Portuguese police of attacking them.
But Passos denied on Thursday that his men had used excessive force, saying that they had acted to contain a dangerous situation.

British officials declined to comment further until they had received the police report of the incidents which erupted as some United fans tried to leave the stadium shortly before the end of the game, ignoring official instructions to stay put.
"We are urgently seeking a police report from the Portuguese authorities," a British Foreign Office spokesman said in London.
Passos said police had fired plastic pellets and small rubber balls -- both part of anti-riot equipment -- to contain United fans seeking to break out of the stadium.
He said a couple of flares were fired at police ranks.
Police and Manchester United officials had told the fans to remain inside the ground after the game so that they could be taken to buses waiting to ferry them to the airport.
The police chief said the trouble had started among the same group of fans that had earlier clashed with police outside the ground before the game when many of them arrived with invalid tickets.
A number of people were slightly injured in scuffles before police eventually let the group of fans into the stadium.
"These were the same people who caused the problems at the end. They were hooligans," Passos said.
He said 18 police officers had been injured in the various incidents, although none of them seriously. No arrests were made.
The match ended 0-0 but Manchester United went through 4-0 on aggregate after trouncing Porto at Old Trafford.

United become the first English side to reach the last four of Europe's top European club competition since 1985. On that occasion Liverpool reached the final but lost 1-0 to Juventus in a game that went ahead after the Heysel stadium tragedy. Thirty-nine Italian fans died after Liverpool followers rioted.
